story.title: From industrial robots to AI systems
paragraphs: I started programming in 2012, on microprocessors. Before that, and alongside it, there was art, photography, science, marketing, psychology, and robotics. I have studied a lot of things, and never to collect titles. I want to know how things work, and that curiosity does not always know where to stop. It is the reason I can walk into so many rooms and follow what is happening in them.

The robots nearly got me. I trained in automation because I wanted to build and fix actual robots, and what I found was maintenance, keeping machines that already existed alive, in a job that was less than advertised. I sat with that disappointment, and when the offers it promised never came, I jumped. I have been building software ever since, and the years in front of broken machines left me with the two habits I rely on most: patience with broken things, and looking at what nobody is looking at.

Today I balance Stibo STEP master data at Bosch with a master's in Artificial Intelligence, and I still chase the same understanding: psychology, philosophy, art, sci-fi, and the way machines see the world. It is not random interest. The method of one field keeps explaining the other. Observe the system first. Then act.
